text:
maria: heads-up — last night we had ~30% spot preemptions in us-west1 during the 02:00 traffic spike. Several inference pods got drained and cold-starts pushed tail latencies to 1.2s for a few minutes. :grimacing:
kevin: ouch. do we know if those were provider-wide or just specific instance types?
ashish: looks instance-type specific. logs show a bunch of `preemptible-v100-16gb` terminations, others fine.
maria: want to revisit autoscaler defaults for spot-backed pools. current settings: scale_out_cpu=70, cooldown=60s, max_surge=10%. Not great for inference workloads.
kevin: agreed. CPU-based triggers are noisy for inference. I think we should switch to request-queue-depth + p50/p95 request latency as primary signals. short windows (15s) for p95.
nora: also consider a small "hot buffer" of prewarmed on-demand/dedicated instances per pool in each region. keeps the tail down when spot drains. cost hit should be small if sized correctly.
maria: curious about cooldown semantics — when spot nodes vanish we often get cascading scale-outs because cooldown expired and new nodes immediately trigger another scale. need surge controls + a backoff multiplier.
tim: here's a config proposal I tested in staging, rough example:
```
autoscaler:
  scale_mode: mixed_capacity
  signals:
    - name: inference_queue_depth
      target: 120   # requests per node
    - name: p95_latency_ms
      target: 200
  scale_up:
    stabilization_window: 15s
    cooldown: 90s
    max_surge: 0.25    # allow 25% extra capacity during ramp
    backoff_multiplier: 1.5
  scale_down:
    cooldown: 300s
    min_ready_replicas: 2
  preemption_handling:
    grace_seconds: 30
    drain_timeout: 45s
    fallback_policy: route_to: dedicated_pool
```
kevin: nice. i like `max_surge` instead of immediate full-scale. that avoids over-alloc when spot returns stale metrics. backoff_multiplier helps avoid thrashing.
ashish: add jitter to cooldowns so multiple pools don't scale in lockstep on region-wide events. e.g., cooldown = base +- random(0,15s).
maria: question: fallback_policy routing — do we failover whole requests to dedicated pool or keep them in queue until new spot nodes boot? which is better for latency?
kevin: for latency-sensitive endpoints, failover to dedicated immediately. for best-effort batch jobs, hold in queue. we should make per-route policy configurable.
nora: region constraints: some regions have tiny dedicated quotas, so we should have cross-region routing as last resort. but that has higher latency. document tradeoffs for SRE & product teams.
ashish: also enforce a per-AZ cap for spot usage to avoid single-AZ blowups. mixed_capacity pools need an AZ-aware placement policy.
maria: can we add a short circuit: if preemption_rate > 20% for 2m, reduce spot target and scale up dedicated by X replicas with a linear ramp over 60s? less noisy than instant swap.
tim: yeah, implemented a hysteresis rule in the staging scaler: when preempt_rate > 0.2 over 120s -> reduce desired_spot_pct by 30% and trigger dedicated ramp with `ramp_seconds: 60`. it smoothed the tail in tests.
kevin: cost check — what does that mean in $/hour for a typical pool of 40 gpus? rough math: if dedicated gpus are 3x spot price, moving 30% (12 gpus) is 12*(dedicated_cost - spot_cost). for us that's ~12*(3-1)=24 units (very rough), but it prevents latency SLO violations which are more costly.
maria: good enough for a rough risk discussion. ops: can we get a runbook entry that spells thresholds and oncall actions? if the autoscaler triggers fallback twice in 30m, page the infra owner. @oncall: FYI.
autoscale-bot: [staging] deployed autoscaler config `mixed-capacity-v3` to cluster stg-inference-2 at 1775012399 :rocket:
maria: thanks. let's watch the canary during the next traffic window (tonight). can someone add a dashboard: preempt_rate, spot_pct, desired_spot_pct, p95_latency, queue_depth, dedicated_ramp_events?
nora: i'll add a dashboard and a short doc with the tradeoffs + per-route settings.
kevin: small note — remember GC/eviction spikes when several nodes drain at once. we should run a quick test where we simulate N node preempts in parallel and verify drains don't exceed `drain_timeout`.
ashish: created a quick repro script in staging cluster: `scripts/simulate-preempt.sh` (uses cordon+delete loop). logs show graceful reassignments in 90% of cases, 10% had cold starts > 1s.
maria: ok, plan: tonight deploy to production with `max_surge=0.2`, `cooldown=90s +- jitter`, `fallback_policy=dedicated_ramp(30%,60s)`, monitor dashboard, page infra owner if fallback >=2 in 30m.
kevin: :thumbsup:
tim: will push the k8s autoscaler CRD change at 1775012440, tagging the rollout.
autoscale-bot: [prod] rollout started for `mixed-capacity-v3` at 1775012445 (canary 5%)
maria: tagging this thread as reference for the runbook. @everyone, please add any missing edge cases here. :eyes:
